2.0.0.en: 1 Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand; 2 A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations. 3 A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them. 4 The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run. 5 Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array. 6 Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness. 7 They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: 8 Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded. 9 They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief. 10 The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: 11 And the LORD shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the LORD is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?

2.0.1.en: The people did not benefit from the locust raids, for it was said by the prophet Amos: “I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD” (Amos 4:9). So he began to speak to them of another chastening, the destructive raids of enemies, saying:

2.0.2.en: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand. [1]

2.0.3.en: First: blowing the trumpet in Zion. Sounding trumpets was part of the very work of the priests; they were sounded when the procession moved “in the wilderness,” at the announcement of war, at the anointing of the king, at the celebration of feasts, etc... The trumpet was of silver (Lev 10) and points to the divine commandment or the divine word, which works in the soul during its striving and its war against sin and fills it with joy and gladness with every inner divine work.

2.0.4.en: God commands the blowing of the trumpet in Zion not because a particular nation is attacking Zion, but because the day of the LORD is coming, so that all the inhabitants of the land tremble... It is a near day!!

2.0.5.en: Perhaps by the blowing of trumpets in Zion, on the holy mountain, He wanted to declare that it is God who permits the enemies to rage against His people to chasten them. If they do not listen to His voice through the commandment, He brings them terror through their enemies, using them to accomplish their deliverance from evil; they did not listen to His meekness, so let them await His firmness!

2.0.6.en: Let us hear the sound of the trumpet, God's warnings, from the mouth of the priests, and let us accept the divine commandment even if it is bitter to the wicked, because it shatters the evil they love, for “all the inhabitants of the land tremble”; everything earthly is shaken in the heart of the wicked before the divine commandment, and every transgression and trespass within him quakes before it. As it was said: “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?!” (Amos 3:6).

2.0.7.en: If the blowing of the trumpet points to the coming of the divine Word to the soul, this is necessarily followed by the shattering of every inner idol that has occupied the heart for a time, as Isaiah the prophet says: “Behold, the LORD rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it” (Isa 19:1).

2.1.0.en: Second: “A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains” [2].

2.1.1.en: If the day of the Lord for true believers is a joyful and radiant wedding day, when the Bridegroom, the Sun of Righteousness, comes forward to meet His bride who shines like the moon with His light, then for the wicked it is a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, for they cannot behold the Lord in His glory and splendor, nor enjoy His mysteries.

2.1.2.en: The prophet Joel looks at the periods of the locust invasion and sees the sky turned into pitch darkness, not because the sun is absent, but because of the locusts that covered the whole sky, so that man lost the sight of the light, and day turned to night in his eyes. This scene was described in the Book of Exodus at the plague of locusts on the land of Egypt: “And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt... For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened” (Ex 10:14-15).

2.1.3.en: Through this scene the prophet Joel saw what would happen in Judah by the armies of the enemies. Because of the multitude of the fighting army and the chariots, the land of Judah turns into a dust storm causing gloom and darkness. In the same image the matter is fulfilled for the wicked on the great day of the Lord, when He comes to judge the world, so that for them it is gloom and darkness because of the gloom of sin and its darkness which they carried within them, which veils from them the sight of His splendor.

2.1.4.en: Perhaps the darkness and gloom point to the bitterness and distress that come upon the soul during chastening, so that man's eyes and his outlook on life are darkened!

2.1.5.en: As for His saying “as the morning spread upon the mountains,” it means the assurance of its happening. It is coming without fail for all men: the holy mountains and the unclean mountains. The holy mountains of Zion rejoice in it, and the mountains bearing the altars of Baal tremble before it!

2.1.6.en: Third: He presents to us a bitter and harsh picture of the opposing army in respect of the number of the fighters, their strength and their effectiveness, for He describes it thus: 1. “A great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations” [2]. 2. God in His longsuffering waits and is patient... but out of His love He is compelled to chasten. And when we do not respond, God seems harsh in His chastenings, so that when we fall under chastening we feel that it is unique in its pains and bitterness! It is the tender fatherhood for the salvation of the rebellious soul that is dying in its sins!

2.2.0.en: B. It does not stop at the multitude of numbers, but “the appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run. Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap” [4-5]. He terrifies our eyes with its appearance, our ears with its voice. The eyes that found sin pleasant, slack in their spiritual striving, are terrified by the divine chastening, which they see as a violent horse that none can resist, and as horsemen running, so there is no time for slackness or delay. Its voice is dreadful and violent in the extreme, like the noise of chariots that reaches the tops of mountains; none escapes from it!

2.2.1.en: C. As for the work of the chastening, it exposes the work of sin in us. For it turns our inner garden into a wilderness: “A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them” [3]. This fiery invasion, although in its depths it is a divine chastening, is the natural fruit of the work of sin, the destroying fire; whoever practices it embraces a fire that destroys him. This fire can be overcome only by the fire of the Holy Spirit, who turns the desolate wilderness into a joyful paradise. For by the fire of the Holy Spirit the fire of sin is destroyed, and by the fruit of the Spirit the heart is restored to its first state to become the joyful garden of God, so that the believer says to his Savior: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” (Song 4:6).

2.2.2.en: If this book is the book of the dreadful day of the Lord for sinners whose paradise has turned into a wilderness, it is at the same time the book of the outpouring of the Spirit on the sons of men, who restores our nature to us and makes us a paradise for God instead of the wilderness we have become. For this reason St. Gregory bishop of Nyssa says to the catechumens shortly before their baptism: [You are outside paradise, O catechumens. You share with Adam your first father in his exile, and now the door is opened and you return to where you went out from].

2.3.0.en: If the prophet sees in sin a fire consuming stubble [5], then the fiery Spirit turns these ashes into a holy temple of the Lord. St. Cyril the Great says: [The baptized receives the Holy Spirit in him and truly bears the title of temple of God].

2.4.0.en: D. As for the plan, it is extremely well ordered: “they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded” [7-8]. For the prophet saw the locust raids covering the sky completely. They set out to the fields and ate everything green in them, and crept into the houses through the windows. None can resist! And with all this he realized that each locust had its task for which it was sent. So no locust crowds its sister, nor moves except as far as God allowed it for the chastening. What happened was not a mere natural disaster without purpose, but carried a precise purpose in its whole as in its details. And the very same thing is repeated with the invasion of the enemies against Judah: the devastation that occurs is not without purpose, but everything is determined with the utmost precision!

2.4.1.en: God, who permitted the enemy to attack His people, is not hindered by the wall standing before him; the plan is accomplished and each enters his position, and if he falls among the weapons he is not wounded until he fulfills the purpose.

2.4.2.en: E. None escapes this chastening, since all have sinned. If it attacks the open fields in the villages and turns them into a wilderness, it creeps like thieves through the windows into the houses in the cities. It leaps over the wall and no barrier stands before it... None can flee, for the fruit of sin follows him wherever he is, even if he is inside his chamber surrounded by impregnable walls!

2.5.0.en: F. It carries the bitterness of myrrh, and none can bear it: “The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: and the LORD shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the LORD is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?! [10-11].

2.5.1.en: These are the very signs the Lord Christ Himself gave concerning His last coming; they are terrifying signs for wicked sinners... God permits nature to be shaken and to tremble before them so that they may realize what sin does to nature, and sinners prepare by repentance to meet the Lord.

2.5.2.en: And it is wonderful that God regards the army opposing His people as “His army,” because it is He who permitted it to carry out the chastening, so that it became His rod for chastening, but only for a time.

2.5.3.en: The Fathers have spiritual, symbolic understandings of the quaking of the earth, the trembling of the heavens, the darkening of the sun and moon and the falling of the stars... a matter to which we return at greater length in our study of the Gospel of Matthew (Mt 24), God willing and if we live, being content here with a few excerpts:

2.5.4.en: * Now is the end of all the passing life. As the Apostle says, the fashion of this outward world passes away, to be followed by a new world, and instead of the visible stars Christ Himself shines as the sun of the new creation and its king. Great is the power of this new sun. And great is His splendor, like the sun that now shines, where the moon and the other stars grow dark before this great light.

2.5.5.en: Eusebius of Caesarea * Just as the moon and the stars quickly dwindle before the rising sun, so before the appearing of Christ the sun is darkened, and the moon does not give its light, and the stars fall from heaven, so that their former splendor is taken from them that they may put on the garment of the great light.

2.5.6.en: St. John Chrysostom The trembling earth is the body, which grows weak and wasted before the abominations that man commits for the delight and ease of his body, so that while he thinks he is giving his body rest, he makes it tremble without knowing. And the heavens point to the soul, which should have been the center of the Kingdom of God and the place of His dwelling... The soul loses its security and peace through sin, and so trembles. And the heavenly lights cease, a sign of the loss of spiritual sight and entrance into a state of spiritual confusion. Thus the divine chastening declares the fruit of our sins; it exposes them in us, so that we cannot bear His dreadful day. The men of Beth-shemesh, who had looked into the ark of the covenant, said earlier: “Who is able to stand before this holy LORD God? and to whom shall he go up from us?” (1 Sam 6:20). As the psalmist says: “Thou, even thou, art to be feared: and who may stand in thy sight when once thou art angry? Thou didst cause judgment to be heard from heaven; the earth feared, and was still, when God arose to judgment, to save all the meek of the earth” (Ps 76:7-9).

2.6.0.en: 12 Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: 13 And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil. 14 Who knoweth if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering unto the LORD your God? 15 Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: 16 Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet. 17 Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O LORD, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?

2.6.1.en: Having revealed through His chastenings the working of sin in soul and body, God opened wide the doors of hope to His people so that none should fall into despair. For He calls, saying: “Turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: and rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil. Who knoweth if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering unto the LORD your God?” [12-14].

2.6.2.en: In this call He declares the following:

2.6.3.en: A. Repentance in its essence is “a return to God”... not merely remorse for sin or ceasing from iniquity, but in its positive aspect a return to the divine embrace, so that we give God the face and not the back... For this reason God affirms His own traits in His relationship with us: that He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and of great mercy.

2.6.4.en: As St. Cyprian says: [He can pardon, having compassion on the sinner who works while asking mercy]. God has used every possible means to express His love for man and His compassion for him so that he may return to Him and find in Him the fatherly embrace that is never closed before those who return! St. Ambrose says: [Let no one fear destruction, whatever his condition and however great his fall, for the good Samaritan of the Gospel will pass by him, and find him going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, that is, fleeing from the sufferings of martyrdom to enjoy the pleasures of the world, wounded by thieves... lying half dead; this good Samaritan, who is a symbol of the Lord Christ, who is the guardian of souls, will not leave you, but will have compassion on you and heal you].

2.6.5.en: If it is God who permits the chastening, which we regard as evil, then when we return to Him “he repenteth him of the evil.” As Father Theodore says: [Scripture is accustomed to use certain expressions in other than their original meaning, so it uses the word “evils” for “sorrows and afflictions,” not because they are evil or evil in nature, but because those upon whom these things come for their good regard them as evil. So when the divine judgment speaks with men, it speaks with them according to their language and human feelings].

2.6.6.en: B. Returning with all the heart: many return to God in time of distress but not with all the heart, so that when the distress is lifted they return at once to their former wickedness, and perhaps to a worse state, as was Pharaoh, who called Moses and Aaron and asked them to pray for him and his people, that he would let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD (Ex 8:8), but “when Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said” (Ex 8:15)...

2.6.7.en: Let our return to God be with all the heart, supported in this by fasting, weeping and mourning... It is as though the body shares with the soul in returning to God, declaring this by prayer, fasting and tears.

2.6.8.en: On this St. Ambrose says: [Would that those who repent knew how to offer repentance, with what zeal and what feelings, and how it swallows up all his thinking, shakes his inner bowels, and pierces the depths of his heart, for Jeremiah the prophet says: “Behold, O LORD; for I am in distress: my bowels are troubled; mine heart is turned within me” (Lam 1:2)].

2.6.9.en: And he says: [“The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground. Mine eyes do fail with tears, my bowels are troubled, my liver is poured upon the earth” (Lam 2:10-11). So also the people of Nineveh grieved and so escaped the destruction of their city (Jonah 3:5). How great is the power of this medicine of repentance, so that it seems to change the intention of God!].

2.6.10.en: [Show your wounds to the Physician and He will heal you... Remove the traces of your wounds with tears! For this is what the woman mentioned in the Gospel did, and so removed the stench of her sins. She washed her sins by washing the feet of the Savior with her tears].

2.6.11.en: Repentance does not stop at the outward appearance, but must touch the inner heart, the whole heart... “Rend your heart, and not your garments.” As St. Cyprian says: [I ask you, dear brethren, that each one confess his sins which he committed in this world... Let us return to the Lord with all the heart, and express our repentance for our sins by true sorrow, beseeching the mercy of God, that our souls may bow before Him, that our sorrow may intercede before Him, that all our hope may be in Him, for He has told us how to ask Him... Let us return to the Lord with all our heart, and quench His anger and wrath by fasting, weeping and mourning, as He Himself advised us].

2.6.12.en: C. His saying: “Who knoweth if he will return and repent” does not mean uncertainty, but is a sign of standing before God with humbling and contrition, hoping for His mercy; for God asks humility in our repentance, since “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise” (Ps 51:17).

2.7.0.en: He repents, not in the sense of a change of God's mind, but in the sense of love, like a father who chastens his son firmly, pretending to be harsh in the hope that his son will return to him, and so he returns to his son. Even in the moments of his firmness he cannot bear the son's tears. And the sign of his repentance is that he leaves behind the chastening a blessing and not wrath, and accepts from his son the offering and the drink offering as a sign of his good pleasure in him and acceptance of him: “leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering unto the LORD your God” [14].

2.7.1.en: D. Repentance is practiced by the whole community, the elders, the children, the infants, the newly married, the priests and the ministers of the LORD. If sin has extended to all, it is fitting that all take part together, and that the building support one another in the life of repentance.

2.7.2.en: The prophet Jeremiah speaks of what sin did to the infants: “The tongue of the sucking child cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the young children ask bread, and no man breaketh it unto them” (Lam 4:4)... And in God's mercy toward Nineveh the children had their own special regard with Him, for He says: “And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?!” (Jn 4:11).

2.8.0.en: E. The priests share with the people in repentance as ministers of the LORD between the porch and the altar, whose principal work is serving the Lord through the altar, that is, in Christ the Sacrifice. They serve through constant prayer and intercession for the people, saying: “Spare thy people, O LORD, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?!” [17].

2.9.s.en: 3. God has pity on His people:

2.9.0.en: 18 Then will the LORD be jealous for his land, and pity his people. 19 Yea, the LORD will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: 20 But I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, and his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things. 21 Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice: for the LORD will do great things. 22 Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness do spring, for the tree beareth her fruit, the fig tree and the vine do yield their strength. 23 Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month. 24 And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil. 25 And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you. 26 And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you: and my people shall never be ashamed. 27 And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.

2.9.1.en: “Then will the LORD be jealous for his land, and pity his people” [18]... What God permitted His people of suffering was out of His jealousy for His holy land, and His tenderness toward His people who are very dear to Him, for while He chastens, He asks His children to look to Him not as an avenging judge but as a loving Father who longs to rejoice in them and delight in their love for Him. The signs of His fatherly love are:

2.10.0.en: A. If the soul enters a state of hunger, thirst and sickness because of sin, God in His love offers Himself as food, drink and spiritual medicine to it, saying: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen” [19]... It no longer asks the Gentiles, that is, the world, to satisfy its emotion, quench its senses or heal its wounds, but finds in its Bridegroom all satisfaction.

2.10.1.en: St. John Saba addresses God, the source of true satisfaction, saying:

2.10.2.en: [Blessed is he who has forgotten the talk of the world by his talk with You, for from You all his needs are fulfilled!

2.10.3.en: You are his food and his drink!

2.10.4.en: You are his house and his dwelling of rest; into You he enters at all times to be sheltered!

2.10.5.en: You are his sun and his day; by Your light he sees hidden things!

2.10.6.en: You are the Father who begot him!

2.10.7.en: You have given the Spirit of Your Son in him, and the Spirit has given him boldness to ask from You all that is Yours, as a son asks of his father! His talk is with You at all times, for he knows no father but You!].

2.11.0.en: B. When God accomplishes the purpose by the chastening, in that the people return to Him, He judges the opposing people, the army that He used as an instrument of chastening... Why? Because it fell into pride, as the prophet says: “Wherefore it shall come to pass, that when the Lord hath performed his whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of his high looks” (Isa 10:12). The enemy acted arrogantly and thought himself mighty, and did not realize that God was using him to chasten His people. Therefore the Lord humbles him for his arrogance: “I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea (the Dead Sea, east of Judea), and his hinder part (his rear) toward the utmost sea (the western sea), and his stink shall come up, and his ill savour (his foul smell) shall come up, because he hath done great things” [20]...

2.11.1.en: Thus, when he falls into arrogance, the Lord splits him, to shatter his front in the waters of the Dead Sea and his rear at the farthest of the western sea so that they may not be gathered together again, and the smell of his stench rises in every place. All this is because of arrogance, as Isaiah the prophet says: “For he saith, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I am prudent: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have robbed their treasures, and I have put down the inhabitants like a valiant man... Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory he shall kindle a burning like the burning of a fire. And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day; and shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field (soul and body together)” (Isa 10:13-18).

2.12.0.en: C. The Lord washes their former wounds, turning the grief that overcame them because of sin into gladness and joy [21].

2.13.0.en: D. The sanctification of all energies and gifts by the Holy Spirit, for He says: “Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness do spring, for the tree beareth her fruit, the fig tree and the vine do yield their strength. Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the LORD your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month” [22-23].

2.13.1.en: The Messianic age was linked in the minds of the prophets with holy waters (Ezek 36:26; Isa 30:23; Jer 31:9; Zech 13:1-2; Ps 46:4, etc.) that turn the wilderness into fertile land, water the believers like the trees of the paradise of God, remove uncleanness and purify the land from the worship of idols, and bring life and sanctification...

2.13.2.en: What is the former and latter rain but the Holy Spirit who waters the thirsty soul, so that the wilderness springs, the trees bear their fruit, and the fig tree and the vine yield their strength?! It is the Holy Spirit who worked in ancient times as the former rain, but much more settled in us after the Lord's ascension to turn our inner wilderness into a joyful paradise!

2.13.3.en: The prophet says: “Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness do spring.” If the body has become, because of sin, like the beasts of the field without pasture, the Holy Spirit sanctifies the body and satisfies all its energies and senses with what is for edification; He does not destroy the beasts of the field, nor despise their worth, but sanctifies them and satisfies them with what is of the Lord! For this reason He asks the children of Zion to be glad and rejoice because of this heavenly rain. It is as though the prophet declares through the shadow what the Lord said to His disciples: “Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you” (Jn 16:7).

2.13.4.en: This is the rain that the Lord Christ promised His disciples to send them from the Father as a sign of His love for them and care for them, and as it is written in Proverbs: “In the light of the king's countenance is life; and his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain” (Prov 16:15). And Hosea the prophet says: “His going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth” (Hos 6:3). And Zechariah the prophet asks us to ask for this latter rain to work in our lives: “Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain; so the LORD shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field” (Zech 10:1). This is God's great gift: “Let us now fear the LORD our God, that giveth rain, both the former and the latter, in his season: he reserveth unto us the appointed weeks of the harvest” (Jer 5:24).

2.14.0.en: The Lord Christ gave us this latter rain in due time so that our souls may be satisfied with the Lord and praise Him, and realize His dwelling in their midst, that is, He gives them spiritual satisfaction and a life of praise and the sense of the divine presence, for He says: “And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you: and my people shall never be ashamed. And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed” [26-27].

2.14.1.en: Since man went out of paradise hungry, the whole world cannot satisfy his heart or his senses or his mind... so he remains wandering on the face of the earth in great hunger until God fills him with His satisfying Holy Spirit!

2.14.2.en: This satisfaction begets praise, so that man becomes like the infant who rejoices in his mother, so that all his feelings are stirred and all the members of his body respond with his joy to bring forth a song of true love that the tongue cannot express. For praise is not merely words we chant or melodies we learn, but in its depths it is a state of true joy that shakes the whole being of the believer, bodily and spiritually, so that the tongue breaks out in praise, and the heart dances with delight in the Lord, and the whole soul is stirred with heavenly, angelic melodies.

2.14.3.en: This praise is linked with the believer's awareness of the Lord's dwelling in him. He praises and exults not because of the gifts, even if they are spiritual, but because of the Giver Himself, the Giver of gifts!

2.14.4.en: These are the signs of God's fatherly love for His people. He satisfies the soul, waters it, binds up its wounds, restores to it its glory in Him, and removes from it the shame of sin and iniquity, sanctifying all its energies and gifts for His own account, declaring His dwelling in it as the mystery of its satisfaction and its spiritual praise!

2.14.5.en: The blessings of His love for His people can be summarized as follows:

2.14.6.en: A. He pities them, that is, has compassion and tenderness toward them [18].

2.14.7.en: B. He answers them and listens to them [19].

2.14.8.en: C. He satisfies their needs and grants them spiritual satisfaction [19].

2.14.9.en: D. He removes shame from them [19], granting them glory.

2.14.10.en: E. He drives out their enemies and shatters their pride [20].

2.14.11.en: F. He removes from them fear and anxiety [21].

2.14.12.en: G. He gives them gladness and joy [21].

2.14.13.en: H. He cares even for their beasts [22].

2.14.14.en: I. He blesses the fruit of their land [22].

2.14.15.en: J. He gives them the former and latter rain [23] (the gift of the Holy Spirit).

2.14.16.en: K. He compensates them for the years that the locust has eaten [24].

2.14.17.en: L. He gives them the spirit of praise and living spiritual worship [26].

2.14.18.en: M. He declares His wonders in their lives, so that they become a wonder [26].

2.15.0.en: N. He declares His dwelling in their midst [27].

2.16.0.en: O. He gives them His Holy Spirit [28].

2.17.s.en: 4. Radical reform by the Holy Spirit:

2.17.0.en: 28 And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: 29 And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit. 30 And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. 31 The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come. 32 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the LORD hath said, and in the remnant whom the LORD shall call.

2.18.0.en: When God pities His people and is jealous for His inheritance, He withholds nothing from them, but gives them Himself. He gives them His Holy Spirit in them as the mystery of their radical inner change, for He says: “And it shall come to pass (that is, in the last times) that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: and also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit” [29].

2.18.1.en: It is the great gift that God gave to mankind after preparing for it by offering the sacrifice of redemption on the Cross. This gift which the Church enjoyed on the day of Pentecost, as the Apostle Peter declared (Acts 2:14-21), and which was offered to every man who comes to God, is God's gift to sons and daughters, that is, without distinction of sex on the one hand. And on the other hand it is given even to those of little experience, for it is the free gift from God to everyone who receives!

2.18.2.en: And it is God's gift to the old men whose lives have grown slack and who feel lost, for He turns their spiritual old age into youth renewed in the Lord, full of hope and joy.

2.18.3.en: It is God's gift to the servants and handmaids, given to those who realize that they are slaves, so that He frees them, granting them the spirit of sonship.

2.18.4.en: It is God's gift to the sons of men... that is, to all who receive!

2.18.5.en: As for the work of the Holy Spirit in us, it suffices to recall the words of St. Basil the Great: [Through the Holy Spirit is the restoration of our dwelling in paradise.

2.18.6.en: Our ascent to the Kingdom of Heaven.

2.18.8.en: Our boldness to call God “our Father.”

2.18.9.en: Our sharing in the grace of Christ.

2.18.10.en: Our being called sons of light.

2.18.11.en: And in one word, our receiving the fullness of blessing in this age and in the age to come].

2.18.12.en: St. Ambrose comments on the phrase “I will pour out my spirit,” saying: [He did not say “I will pour out the Spirit” but “Of My Spirit,” for we cannot receive the fullness of the Holy Spirit, but we receive as much as our Lord apportions from Himself according to His will (Phil 2:6)]. But this does not mean that the Spirit does not dwell in us, nor that we receive a part of Him, for St. Clement of Alexandria warns us against dividing the Spirit; rather it is the mystery of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, working in us as God wills for our edification, in a surpassing divine manner.

2.19.0.en: This gift is accompanied by: “wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come” [30]... It is as though the goal of this great gift is to launch the Church toward the great day of the Lord, to see heaven and earth pass away, the light of the world put out so that what is divine remains! By this her heart is set ablaze toward union with God alone, the Eternal!

2.20.0.en: Finally he closes his prophecy about the Holy Spirit by declaring His acceptance of all who come to Him from all the nations, for He says: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered” [32]. God opens His arms to everyone who calls on Him, whether Jew or Gentile, as the Apostle Paul says: “For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved” (Rom 10:11-13). And as Peter says: “For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call” (Acts 2:39).

2.20.1.en: St. Augustine says: [The name of the Maker of heaven and earth was formerly called upon among the Israelites alone, while the rest of the nations called upon the dumb, deaf idols that do not hear, or called upon the demons, who hear what is to their harm]. But now the Gentiles have come to call on the name of the living God by the Holy Spirit.

2.21.s.en: In the midst of Your chastenings I feel the tenderness of Your compassion!

2.21.0.en: * You permitted the four locust raids to chasten Your people, and when they did not benefit You sent them the raid of the Babylonians...

2.21.1.en: And in all this You are wonderful in Your love!

2.21.3.en: In the midst of Your chastenings I feel the tenderness of Your compassion!

2.21.4.en: * In the midst of Your chastenings I feel that Your day is a day of gloom, but You are behind the cloud!

2.21.5.en: Soon the cloud will lift and You will shine in me with Your splendor!

2.21.6.en: Allow me to see Your light amid my sufferings!

2.21.7.en: * Teach me how tender You are in Your love and compassion, so that I return to You not by rending my garments but by the contrition of my heart!

2.21.8.en: Against You only have I sinned; to You I disclose the wounds of my soul, O heavenly Physician!

2.21.9.en: Heal me, and I shall be healed!

2.21.10.en: Fill every void of my heart with Your love!

2.21.11.en: Send Your Holy Spirit to work in my depths!

2.21.12.en: Let Him turn my inner wilderness into a heavenly paradise!

2.21.13.en: How tender You are in Your love even in the moments of Your chastening of me!
